subject: Sizing checklist and next steps for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Cameron Thomas <cameron.thomas@quantumretail.com>, Priya Desai <pdesai@quantumretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + sizing asks (Dedicated / Hosted / Private)

Thanks again for the call earlier — great context, Cameron and Priya. Quick recap and a set of concrete asks so we can produce a clean Dedicated sizing recommendation and clarify the Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for your procurement team:

- What we heard (high level):
  * Primary need: low 99th latency for customer-facing search and chat features; batch inference for nightly enrichment jobs.
  * Security: long-term requirement for VPC/private deployment (data residency), but initial POC could run on Redwood Hosted if acceptable for the pilot.
  * Goal: reduce per-token cost relative to current cloud infra while keeping sub-200ms 99th latency for short chat queries.

- Explicit asks (if you can confirm in reply):
  1) Typical sustained TPS during business hours (avg): ____ TPS
  2) Peak TPS during marketing events or Black Friday style spikes (peak): ____ TPS and duration
  3) Concurrency requirement (how many concurrent active sessions should remain low-latency)
  4) Token mix: median/90th/peak request token lengths (e.g., median 50 tokens, 90th 400 tokens, peak 1200 tokens)
  5) % of requests that are batch vs interactive (rough %)
  6) Any hard compliance constraints that require Private on day 1 (SOC2 is fine for us to run Hosted for POC)

I attached our blank capacity worksheet to make #1-5 quick to fill — if you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute sizing workshop with Ben to walk through it. After we have the numbers we'll:
  - produce a Dedicated GPU mix recommendation (GPU types, pool sizes),
  - provide cost delta vs Hosted for the pilot and steady-state, and
  - outline migration path to VPC/on-prem when you’re ready.

Attachments: quantum_capacity_worksheet_v2.xlsx (worksheet stub), session-recording-20261004.mp4 (recording stub)

Thanks — Kim

--

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + sizing asks (Dedicated / Hosted / Private)

On Sun, Oct 4, 2026 at 2:05 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call earlier — great context, Cameron and Priya. Quick recap and a set of concrete asks so we can produce a clean Dedicated sizing recommendation and clarify the Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for your procurement team:

Thanks Kim — appreciate the structure. Filling in the worksheet fields inline below: 

1) Typical sustained TPS (business hours): ~35 TPS (reads+chat generation)
2) Peak TPS: around 120 TPS for ~10-15 minutes during campaigns; longer marketing spikes can hold ~60 TPS for 1-2 hours
3) Concurrency: we need ~250 concurrently active sessions with sub-200ms target for short responses (short = <= 120 tokens)
4) Token mix: median ~60 tokens, 90th ~= 450 tokens; peak single requests for batch enrichment ~1200 tokens (these are ~12-15% of traffic)
5) Batch vs interactive: roughly 15% batch (nightly enrichment), 85% interactive
6) Compliance: We need to be ready to move to Private (VPC) within 3-6 months — SOC2 is acceptable for POC but procurement will require VPC for production.

Extra: Question on GPU flavors — are H100s strongly recommended for latency-sensitive workloads? What tradeoffs would we see with an A100 / A10G mix for cost?

Happy to do the 30-minute workshop; available Tuesday 10/6 between 9-12 PT.

-Cameron

Cameron Thomas
Head of Search & Personalization | Quantum Retail
cameron.thomas@quantumretail.com | +1 (212) 555-0899
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + sizing asks (Dedicated / Hosted / Private)

Kim — quick internal note before we lock the workshop:

- Given the mix Cameron called out (35 sustained, 120 short peaks, 250 concurrency, ~15% long/1200-token jobs), my quick preference would be:
  * Primary pool: H100 (for latency-critical interactive tokens + high throughput per card)
  * Secondary cost pool: A10G or A100s for batch enrichment jobs and lower-priority burst capacity
  * Autoscaling: configure burst pool to kick in at 85% of provisioned TPS for the H100 pool to avoid steady underutilization

- We'll model a 2-tier approach in the worksheet (H100s + A10G) and include both per-token cost and 99th-latency projections.

Linking the GPU tradeoffs doc I use: https://redwood.internal/docs/gpu-tradeoffs (internal)

Ben

Cameron — thanks for the detail, this is perfect and exactly what we needed.

Next steps: 
- Attached: updated worksheet (quantum_capacity_worksheet_v2.xlsx) pre-filled with your numbers; Ben will add GPU-mix scenarios by EOD.
- Proposed workshop: Tue 10/6 10:00-10:30 PT to walk through the worksheet and agree on pilot vs steady-state numbers — does that time work?
- We'll include three deployment path options in the workshop deliverable: Hosted POC (fastest), Dedicated Reserved Pool (predictable performance/cost), Private VPC migration plan (procurement runway + calendar).

Regarding Cameron’s GPU question: Ben will present H100 vs A100/A10G tradeoffs during the call. Short takeaway: H100 gives the best latency headroom for the interactive tier; A10G/A100 are cost-efficient for batch and warm standby. We'll show concrete throughput per-GPU numbers in the model.

If Priya or procurement needs any specific procurement artifacts (SLA language, expected contract term, or an estimated monthly commit), flag that now and we'll have a one-pager ready for the meeting.

Attachments: quantum_capacity_worksheet_v2.xlsx (updated)

Cheers,
Kim
